A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same statistical framework and contain the complete main text and Appendices A–G. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable matching of equations, figures, tables, and software listings.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 30 statistical model configurations on Chatbot Arena data, ranking and clustering analyses, and regressions relating LLM characteristics to scores, including Tables D.1–D.3 and F.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and analyses, including their numerical results in Tables D.1–D.3 and F.1.

M1.justification: The factored tie model, Thurstonian covariance construction, likelihood optimization, and constraints in Section 2 are unchanged. Appendix G changes software class and argument names without changing the stated statistical procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same September 2024 Chatbot Arena data and use the same Epoch AI attributes for Appendix F. The introduction's new mention of sports and marketing describes existing applications, not additional evaluated domains.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons retain the same Bradley–Terry, Rao–Kupper, and Davidson configurations. Listings G.2 and G.3 add standard Bradley–Terry Model 1 to the tutorial examples, but this comparator already appears in the corresponding empirical tables in v1; no reported comparison gains or loses a baseline.

E3.justification: The experimental configurations, optimization settings, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, and 90/10 train-test split in Appendix D remain unchanged. The revised Appendix G interfaces do not establish a change to the reported experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain the covariance and tie-factor comparisons, global-optimizer consistency checks, generalization analysis, ranking and clustering analyses, and characteristic-score regressions. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table F.1 retains the same standard-error and p-value reporting, Figure F.1 retains its 95% confidence bands, and Listing G.3 retains seed 20. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-estimation procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Model 18 retains overall RMSE values of 17.9 in Table D.2 and 55.8 in Table D.3. Figure F.1 changes presentation but preserves its data points, regression curves, and confidence bands.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, and proofs in Section 2 and Appendices B–C are unchanged. Equation (11c) changes only its trailing punctuation from a period to a comma.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: factored tie modeling, covariance-based analysis, optimization constraints, and the leaderbot implementation. Claims about improved fit, ranking interpretation, and broader applicability retain their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of covariance versus tie modeling, parameter non-identifiability, and overfitting at high tie-factor complexity remain unchanged. Appendix F also retains the same caution about sparse information for proprietary models.

D1.justification: Appendix G replaces Factor-suffixed classes and n_cov_factors/n_tie_factors arguments with unified classes and k_cov/k_tie, introduces marginal_outcomes() in the visualization example, and adds Model 1 to two example lists. Data-loading guidance changes from directly obtaining the latest Chatbot Arena dataset to supplying an external dataset URL. These are localized reproducibility-guide updates.

R1.justification: v2 removes Li et al. (2024), Predicting ties in Chatbot Arena: the Rao-Kupper model, from the introduction and bibliography. The associated acknowledgment of prior chatbot applications is replaced with sports and marketing examples pointing to the existing Appendix A; the remaining research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the introduction, Appendix G explanations and code comments, equation punctuation, and the funding acknowledgment, which changes IARPA to DARPA. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure F.1 adjusts model-label placement and legend styling without changing the plotted evidence. Software listings and bibliography undergo limited reflow; the set and organization of figures and tables are preserved.

improvement.justification: Appendix G clarifies external-data loading and expands examples to include standard Bradley–Terry, but its descriptions still say five models after the listings expand to six. v2 also removes an explicit acknowledgment of directly relevant prior chatbot tie-modeling work. With scientific evidence unchanged and the practical benefit of the API replacements unverified by the PDFs, these limited benefits and drawbacks do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
